quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To be ready for hazards on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look constantly at the entire road and its sides.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look constantly at the entire road and its sides.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous traffic situations depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. You need to scan the whole road, including both sides.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park only in legal spots where other drivers can clearly see your parked vehicle.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, the maximum speed limit on freeways is:
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on freeways is 70 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow any posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches you with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights, sirens, or other warning devices, move to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system in your vehicle is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gas from your vehicle and stops fumes from entering the cabin. Keep your exhaust system leak-free to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning. Fix any broken parts right away.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit in residential subdivisions is:
questions.explanation: The speed limit in residential subdivisions is 25 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow any posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
You may pass even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers can pass in both directions. You may only pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Drivers should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than larger vehicles.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many collisions happen because drivers were looking but still did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lighting. Always watch for these smaller, less protected road users.

questions.question: On a two-lane street, a fire engine is following you but not using emergency signals. You should:

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you but not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Continue driving normally.

questions.question: Before turning left, it is important to:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic gets a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes, then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area designated for motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is a large blind spot around trucks and other large vehicles. Avoid staying in these blind spots.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs indicate a school zone. Be alert for children and pedestrians when driving near a school.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when one driver does not see another vehicle or does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is ahead. Enter at a low speed and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning on a residential street. Signal five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, the vehicle will keep moving fast even if you release the gas pedal. Turn off the ignition carefully. Then apply your brakes and move safely off the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people entering the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your blinker before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Decrease the distance between their vehicle and the car ahead.
Increase the distance between their vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between their vehicle and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase your following distance.

questions.question: In bad weather, heavy traffic, or at high speeds, how far behind another vehicle should you stay?
questions.explanation: The more space between your car and others, the more time you have to react. Keep six or more seconds of distance in bad weather and heavy traffic.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: A driver extends their left arm and hand downward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: In normal traffic, how far before turning should you signal?
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes in normal conditions. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: Signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Not following them can result in a penalty.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, what should you do with your front wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a sharp turn is coming and they should slow down.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, which lane should you use?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign drive 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Your car will need more time to stop.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Get closer to the car in front of you.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden speed or direction changes. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, drivers of small vehicles should expect:

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create wind gusts strong enough to push smaller vehicles sideways. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles at high speeds.

questions.question: When is driving below the speed limit illegal?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly and disrupting traffic flow is illegal. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading at you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.

questions.explanation: If a car is heading straight at you, honk to get attention. If they don't move, steer right. Steering left may cause a crash if they correct. Brake firmly. Slowing down reduces impact damage.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow with black symbols or text. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects stopping ability. Slow down on poor roads to keep control. Wet or slippery roads increase stopping distance and risk.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and watch for trains from both directions. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the tracks and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to you, you may pass if:
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you can pass if the road ahead is clear and no cars are coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow diamond warning sign tells you a traffic light is coming. Get ready for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car ahead breaks down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would get in the way of other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you do it safely and do not interfere with other drivers.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What do round signs mean?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is coming. Drive with extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: First, pull up next to the car in front of the space you want. Check traffic and signal before turning your wheels and parking.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right of way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and any pedestrians.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Stay at the scene and identify yourself. Help anyone who needs it.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What is a speed restriction sign?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Speed restriction signs show a recommended speed for curves and turns. Never ignore these signs in bad weather, even if you normally drive faster.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Make you need a tune-up sooner.
Make you feel drowsy while driving.
Start fires in grass on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine. A leak can release dangerous fumes that can make you drowsy or even cause serious harm.
